checks: Verified original §1 (1)–(6). A proper section crosses the simplex interior, so the centroid coordinates are positive. Gamma/radial factorization gives the raw section density 3 f_i and correct threshold stationarity f_i=P_i/t_i.

The cap probability gradient is 3 f_i b in raw coordinates, so the normalized full-row objective weights are P_i^(1/3). The central pair is strictly captured in y and in the complement of x. Reversing orientation negates the Hessian, yielding the two strict signs including equality in the centrality bound.

Normalization to unit threshold multiplies the raw probability Hessian by t_i². Together with the capacity scaling and the normalized weight this gives the exact factor 1/(3 f_i), with distinct shift constants for the two rows allowed.
The feasible transfers on the positive part of the zero row give z_j=w/b_j. Its weighted geometric-mean Hessian on the face is (bbᵀ/3−diag(b_j²))/w, and the pair direction evaluates to −2b_ℓ² b_m²/w.

All three stated velocities sum to zero as a vector and preserve the original zero entry. All other original entries remain positive for sufficiently small t of either sign. Degree-one homogeneity kills the radial and radial-mixed Hessian terms. Completing the square in α gives the strict inequality B>AC/(A+C) and its reciprocal equivalent.

dependencies.mapping: The positive pair ℓ,m has b_ℓ,b_m≤1/3 and both margins strictly positive in y and −c_x. Coarea gives stationary through-centroid cuts, so its exact pair-variation test applies, and complementation reverses the sign for x.

Both full rows are strictly positive with proper optimizing thresholds. Normalize their margin vectors by t_i; b·v=0 makes v tangent to their probability gradients. The accepted shift and Hessian scaling produce κ_i and the weighted raw factor.
The exact one-zero capacity equals the geometric mean on the three positive entries; only tangent motions preserving the hole are used.

overlap.comparison: Corrects one central-pair direction in one positive row after threshold normalization. It does not fund the simultaneous distinct full-row shifts with the one-zero row or include the zero-row curvature cost.
Uses a corrected positive direction for excluding a different stochastic configuration by a joint index argument. It does not calculate the present three-row compensated quadratic.

readability: The proof uses raw probability Hessians for A and B and threshold-normalized Hessians only inside the accepted Schur formula. The condition is an iff for this particular two-parameter direction family.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The two full-row corrections and one-zero row reserve give an exact feasible second variation and the stated strict joint funding criterion.
